text:
IncidentBot: [SEV2] GeoDNS + external resolver amplification detected in eu-west. Paging @oncall-sre :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: I’m up, looking. What’s the hit?
emily: Seeing a big spike in DNS timeouts from eu-west APPS (500s), started ~12:07 UTC. Backend requests fine, but client errors on connect for ~5-10% of requests.
sanjay: Confirmed. Synthetics show resolver latency to Cloudflare edge jumping 2s -> 8s, plus NXDOMAIN flaps.
lisa: Map looks regional — eu-west1 -> high errors, us-east ok. Could be Cloudflare resolver pool or Route53 propagation divergence.
oncall-sre: Quick triage: run dig from eu node and from our healthcheck lambda.
miguel: dig output from eu-prober:
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai +short
(;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached)
```
From us-prober:
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai +short
54.23.12.4
```
eng-runtime: Also seeing increased 5xx in edge logs with upstream connect failures labeled "dns_timeout".
oncall-sre: OK. Likely external resolver saturation or Cloudflare anycast steering issue. Steps: 1) Failover GeoDNS weights away from eu-cloudflare edge pool to Route53 backup for eu. 2) Add conservative TTL override for next 10m. 3) Add resolver fallback in infra (1.1.1.1 -> 8.8.8.8) via iptables/ndots? 4) Open ticket with Cloudflare.
emily: I can push a GeoDNS weight change now — lowering Cloudflare pool to 10% and raising Route53 pool to 90% for eu. Anyone object?
sanjay: Do it. Also annotate in status page (I’ll start draft).
eng-runtime: Pushing route change: ``routemgr update geo eu set weights cloudflare=10,route53=90 --dry-run`` then apply.
miguel: Applied. Propagation started at 12:18 UTC. TTL was 60s, changed to 30s.
oncall-sre: Adding resolver fallback to infra: pushing config to edge nodes to prefer 8.8.8.8 when 1.1.1.1 times out twice. Rolling to 10% of hosts to test.
lisa: Customer impact: spike in 5xx on EU-facing apps. Top customers affected: client-a (EU), client-b (DE). I’m pinging CSMs.
emily: Status page update draft: "We are investigating increased DNS errors impacting a subset of EU traffic. Mitigation in progress (GeoDNS weight adjustment and resolver fallbacks)." @sanjay add timings?
sanjay: Posted initial status at 12:22 UTC.
cloudflare-support-bot: Ticket #CF-48234 created with Cloudflare support (sent at 12:20 UTC). Case notes: high resolver latency + occasional timeouts from eu-pop.
oncall-sre: Monitoring: error rate down from 9% -> 3% since weight change. Latency back to ~300ms. Still seeing intermittent NXDOMAINs.
miguel: We added an extra retry on client side (2 -> 4) to mask transient DNS failures; rollout 30% -> 100% in 20m.
lisa: CSMs acknowledged, proactively emailed top 5 EU customers. No SLA breaches expected if rate stays <5% for 1h, will keep them updated.
emily: Cloudflare replied: "Investigating routing anomaly in eu-west pop; will update." They asked for PCAPs — uploaded.
eng-runtime: Retention logs attached to ticket, plus traceroutes. Also collected tcpdump from failed connect.
oncall-sre: Handoff: I’ll stay for 40m then hand to @sanjay for the overnight shift. Current state: mitigation applied, error rate reduced but not fully resolved, Cloudflare investigating.
sanjay: ACK. Will monitor and escalate to AWS Route53 if divergence continues. Also preparing a rollback plan to revert GeoDNS if it causes new issues.
emily: Final note: keep TTL at 30s for 15m then raise to 60s if stable.
cloudflare-support-bot: CF update at 12:45 UTC: "Root cause suspected BGP steering misadvertisement, partial traffic blackholing to resolver pool. Mitigation in progress."
oncall-sre: Good. If CF mitigates, we should gradually shift weights back.
lisa: Internal post-incident: collect timeline, affected customer list, and action items (GeoDNS playbook update). Assigning follow-ups to miguel (retries), emily (geo-dns runbook), and oncall-sre (postmortem).
miguel: noted.
sanjay: Taking over monitoring. If error >5% for 15m I will open Route53 escalation.
oncall-sre: handing to @sanjay now. Signing off. :wave:
